H1.claim: The prompt may not contain enough information to deduce the correct value.
H1.why: A1 and A2 were not run; A3 shows only that this specific oracle-derived type/length hint was insufficient; A4 reveals the complete fixed implementation and is not an identifying manipulation of public specification quality. Current evidence neither supports nor rejects natural-language specification insufficiency.

H2.why: Phase 2 showed input-choice and assertion-form changes. Whether SFT improves fixed-input value prediction is schema-dependent and unresolved (Phase 3A v3). Causal support still requires a valid Phase 4 objective intervention.

adapter_or_parameter_capacity_causal.statement: LoRA rank, adapter capacity, full fine-tuning and parameter count as causal factors are untested; the two checkpoints differ in scale and learned representation together.

model_scale_association.statement: Within the Qwen2.5-Coder family, 7B beats 1.5B on this fixed-input panel (A0 +11.46, CI [6.46, 16.67]; A4 +24.79, CI [19.38, 30.42]; recomputed answer-rate gate passed).

H3.why: 7B beats 1.5B on this panel; no causal parameter-count or capacity claim.

H4.why: On exposed functions the SFT effect is -1.67 points under assertion-prefill and +5.00 under the ANSWER schema; the route-exact rule stops at the exposed schema check. Distribution shift is untested: no external diagnostic cohort exists.

H5.why: Syntactic/structural contract degradation only; semantic validity unresolved.

H6.why: Progressive degradation after step 100 only; a rapid early shift or forgetting remains open.

H7.why: An uncertainty/power diagnosis (Kill@8 +3.43, clustered CI [-4.03, 10.88]); not proof of a positive final effect.

numerical_changes: none in any primary or stratum estimate; four exploratory 3C subgroup intervals move by <= 0.3 points (subgroup-only resampling, documented in the 3C v3 receipt)
